evals.prompt: Use three agents to work out whether we should move our event pipeline to the new queue everyone says is three times faster. Four articles report the same figure; one user reports a slower result with durability on, which we require.
evals.expected_output: Writes the target and two to four rivals before reading, including one that rejects the premise. Dispatches blind lanes whose reports are claim lines with origin, rung and setup and no recommendation. Groups the four articles under one origin, rates the vendor figure observed-elsewhere because durability was off, keeps the user's durable-mode measurement as a separate origin, and reports a decision with Rests on, Ruled out, Not verified and Next check.

evals.prompt: Three agents looked into whether upgrading fixes the duplicate-job bug for us. One says the maintainer verified it, one says staging reproduced the fix, one found that production connects through a pooler in a mode the others did not test. Merge their findings.
evals.expected_output: Does not count two agreeing agents as two confirmations. Re-rates both 'verified' and 'reproduced' as observed-elsewhere because neither ran on the production connection mode, joins the mechanism from one lane with the target setup from another, and holds: states what is established, what is not verified on the target, and the cheapest check that would raise the rung.

evals.prompt: Investigate with several agents whether we can roll the setting out to the remaining nodes. It has run on one production node with the same hardware and workload for three weeks with the problem gone and no regressions; several blog posts also recommend it, all quoting the vendor.
evals.expected_output: Notes the blog posts share one origin and sets them aside, finds the crux observed-on-target with nothing contradicting it, and commits plainly: Next check is 'none needed' and no extra investigation is demanded before the rollout.

evals.prompt: This host has no subagents. Work out why signups dropped right after the pricing redesign and whether to roll it back.
evals.expected_output: Runs the same steps alone: frames the target and rivals first, including a rival that the drop is not real, reads the evidence once writing claim lines before forming a view, tests the leading rival against when the effect started, where it appeared and when it stopped, and reports with the same block.

evals.prompt: What is the default port for PostgreSQL?
evals.expected_output: Does not trigger: a lookup with one authoritative source is out of scope, so the question is answered directly with no lanes and no ledger.
